connectors.name: gcal
connectors.title: Google Calendar
connectors.description: Read, create, update and delete Google Calendar events, and find free time: list agendas, fetch event details, make scheduling changes, and search for open slots of a given length across calendars.
connectors.instructions: Find events with listEvents before updating or deleting them; event IDs come from there. Times are RFC 3339 with timezone offsets. Use findFreeTime to propose open slots of a given length instead of scanning agendas by hand.

connectors.name: gcontacts
connectors.title: Google Contacts
connectors.description: Manage Google Contacts the way agents work: contact-shaped tools that finish in one call. Reads return flat contacts (plain emails/phones lists, one organization) instead of raw Person JSON; writes resolve etags and label names internally, so updating a contact or syncing a label's members never needs a lookup first.
connectors.instructions: Find people with searchContacts (across all fields) or getContactByEmail (exact address; fails clearly on zero or several matches). Every contact read returns a shaped contact — plain emails/phones/address lists and one organization — never the raw People API shape. updateContact replaces whole fields: send the complete email/phone list you want to keep. The etag the API requires is resolved inside the connector. Labels resolve by name or resource name in every group tool; modifyGroupMembers adds and removes in one call and answers the new member count. Other contacts are Google's auto-collected addresses, separate from your contacts: list them with listOtherContacts, promote one with copyOtherContact. The Workspace directory is not covered (it needs an extra scope).

connectors.name: gdocs
connectors.title: Google Docs
connectors.description: Read, create and edit Google Docs with task-shaped tools: read a document as plain text, create a document with content, and apply typed edits in one batch.
connectors.instructions: Read the document with readDocument before editing so the structure you edit is current. Compose changes with editDocument, which applies typed edits in one batch; createDocument takes the initial content along. One call per outcome — never hand-roll multi-request sequences.

connectors.name: gdrive
connectors.title: Google Drive
connectors.description: Manage Google Drive files and folders: search files, read file content and metadata, create files and folders, upload content, rename, move, trash, copy, permanently delete, and share.
connectors.instructions: Find files with searchFiles before reading or modifying them; file IDs come from there. readFile returns content, getFile returns metadata. updateFile renames, moves and replaces content; shareFile manages permissions; deleteFile trashes by default.

connectors.name: gforms
connectors.title: Google Forms
connectors.description: Work with Google Forms the way agents work: task-shaped tools that finish in one call. Creating a form takes its questions along, questions are added/edited/deleted by ID or by title (resolved inside the connector), and responses come back with answers keyed by question title — no multi-call choreography.
connectors.instructions: createForm takes the form's questions along — describe them with simple types (text, paragraph, multipleChoice, checkboxes, dropdown, scale, date, time). Questions resolve by ID or title in later calls. getResponses keys answers by question title; publishForm makes the form accept responses.

connectors.name: github-pat
connectors.title: GitHub (token)
connectors.description: Work with GitHub through outcome-oriented tools: repositories, branches, commits, files, issues, pull requests and Actions workflow runs.
connectors.instructions: Repositories are addressed as owner/name. Prefer readFile for file content (decoded text, binaries flagged) and listDirectory for browsing — writeFile and deleteFile resolve SHAs internally. getIssue includes comments and getPull includes changed files. Use proposeChanges for the full edit-branch-open-PR flow in one call; only mergePull when the user explicitly asks to merge.

connectors.name: gitlab-pat
connectors.title: GitLab (token)
connectors.description: Work with GitLab through task-shaped tools, authenticated with a personal access token: propose multi-file changes as merge requests, read and write files, and manage projects, branches, commits, issues, merge requests and pipelines.
connectors.instructions: Projects are addressed by numeric ID or URL-encoded namespace/path; resolve them with listProjects first. Use proposeChanges to open a merge request carrying multi-file changes in one call. This connector authenticates with a personal access token: it can only touch what the token's scopes allow, so a 'not found' on a project you know exists usually means the token lacks access.

connectors.name: gitlab
connectors.title: GitLab
connectors.description: Work with GitLab through task-shaped tools: propose multi-file changes as merge requests, read and write files, and manage projects, branches, commits, issues, merge requests and pipelines.
connectors.instructions: Projects are addressed by numeric ID or URL-encoded namespace/path; resolve them with listProjects first. Use proposeChanges to open a merge request carrying multi-file changes in one call, and readFile/writeFile for direct file work.

connectors.name: gmail
connectors.title: Gmail
connectors.description: Agent-first Gmail: search and read mail with full bodies in one call, send, reply and forward without hand-building MIME, manage drafts, organize mail by outcome (archive, trash, mark read, ...), fetch attachments, and manage labels.
connectors.instructions: Search with Gmail query syntax via searchEmails, then readThread for the whole conversation in one call. sendEmail, replyToEmail and forwardEmail send immediately — use saveDraft when the user should review first. organizeEmail archives, trashes or marks read by outcome; prefer archiving over trashing, and never permanently delete what the tools do not offer.

connectors.name: gsheets
connectors.title: Google Sheets
connectors.description: Read, write and manage Google Sheets with task-shaped tools: read ranges or whole tables, update cells, append rows, clear ranges, create spreadsheets with their initial data, inspect structure, and batch updates.
connectors.instructions: Read before writing: use getValues or readTable to see the current data, then updateValues for targeted edits or appendValues for new rows. Ranges use A1 notation. createSpreadsheet takes the initial data along, so a new spreadsheet rarely needs a second call. Prefer the task-shaped tools over batchUpdate unless you are composing a genuinely custom request.

connectors.name: gslides
connectors.title: Google Slides
connectors.description: Read, create and edit Google Slides presentations: summaries, slides, text, images, reordering and thumbnails.
connectors.instructions: Read before editing: start with getPresentation for the slide list and getSlide for element details, so the structure you edit is current. Prefer the task-shaped tools: addSlide writes title and body in one call, setSlideText rewrites placeholders, and addImage takes sizes in inches. Use batchUpdate only for edits the task tools do not cover, like shapes, tables, or text styling.

connectors.name: gtasks
connectors.title: Google Tasks
connectors.description: Manage Google Tasks the way agents work: task-shaped tools that finish in one call. Lists and tasks are found by ID or by title (resolved inside the connector), so adding, completing, moving, or editing a task never needs a separate lookup first.
connectors.instructions: Lists and tasks resolve by ID or title — pass whichever you have. Complete tasks with completeTask rather than deleting them; use moveTask to reorder or reparent. clearCompletedTasks is destructive, so prefer completing tasks individually when the list itself matters.

connectors.name: outlook-mail
connectors.title: Outlook Mail
connectors.description: Agent-first Outlook Mail (Microsoft 365): search and read mail with full bodies in one call, send, reply and forward, manage drafts, organize mail by outcome (archive, delete, mark read, ...), fetch attachments, and work across shared mailboxes.
connectors.instructions: listMessages browses one folder (a well-known name like inbox, drafts, sentitems, deleteditems or archive, or a folder id) without bodies; searchMessages searches every folder with a KQL-style query (e.g. from:boss@contoso.com subject:invoice hasAttachments:true) and returns full bodies, killing list-then-get round-trips. getMessage reads one message with its full body. sendMessage sends immediately — use saveDraft when the user should review first. replyToMessage replies in one call (replyAll for everyone); forwardMessage forwards. organizeMessage archives, deletes (moves to Deleted Items, recoverable — never permanent), marks read/unread, or moves messages by outcome. getAttachment downloads a file by id or name. Every mail tool takes an optional mailbox (default "me"); pass a shared or delegated mailbox address explicitly — only the signed-in mailbox is discoverable. Message ids can change when a message moves folders, so re-list after moving.
